title: Prospective Study to Evaluate the Clinical Utility of ctDNA Tumor Fraction (TF) for Detection of Estrogen Receptor 1 (ESR1) Mutations in (Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor) HR+/HER2- Metastatic Breast Cancer (MBC)
official: Prospective Study to Evaluate the Clinical Utility of ctDNA Tumor Fraction (TF) for Detection of ESR1 Mutations in HR-positive HER2-negative Metastatic Breast Cancer (MBC)
summary: This is a prospective, single center, single-arm interventional study to evaluate the clinical utility of protocol-mandated diagnostic testing algorithm incorporating liquid biopsy and reflex tissue biopsy NGS for detection of ESR1 mutations in HR+/HER- metastatic breast cancer.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of metastatic breast cancer that is hormone receptor-positive (ER≥10%), HER2 low or negative (defined as HER2 Imunohistochemistry (IHC) 0, 1+ or IHC 2+/In Situ Hybridization (ISH)-).
* Progression of metastatic breast cancer that is hormone receptor-positive (ER≥10%), HER2 low or negative (defined as HER2 IHC 0, 1+ or IHC 2+/ISH-) while on systemic therapy.
* Currently receiving or have previously received aromatase inhibitor therapy.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Patients with locally or regionally recurrent breast cancer without evidence of metastatic disease.
* De novo metastatic breast cancer.
* Presence of symptomatic metastatic visceral crisis.
* Participants with inflammatory breast cancer.
* Intact uterus with a history of endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia (atypical endometrial hyperplasia or higher-grade lesion).
* Diagnosis of any other malignancy within 5 years before enrollment, except for adequately treated basal cell or squamous cell skin cancer, superficial bladder cancer, carcinoma in situ of the cervix, or second primary breast cancer.
* Other conditions that, in the opinion of the treating investigator, would preclude the patient from meeting the study requirements or interfere with interpretation of study results.
* Pregnant and breastfeeding women are excluded from the study
